Project story · October 2026

Our story

Why we care about
an Education Agent

EDUCATION IN RURAL CHINA

Technology in service
of education

Frank worked for a student-run NGO that used technology to help improve education in rural China.

The NGO raised funds and sent student volunteers from the US, Hong Kong, and China.

FOR OUR OWN KIDS

A product we would love
our children to use

We want to create something great for our own kids: a learning companion that helps them explore their questions and follow their curiosity.

01 / The assumption

Education should become
accessible to every child

≈0

Our target for the marginal cost
of another learning interaction

More curiosity should not require a larger cloud bill.

Run inference on the device so children can keep exploring after models are downloaded.

A direction for the product: the cost of serving one more interaction should trend toward zero.

This is an ambition, not a claim of zero total cost. Devices, energy, downloads, development, and support still have costs.

02 / The learning experience

A word becomes
a conversation

Gemma connects a child’s question with the concept they are exploring.

TextRead a short explanation and ask a follow-up.
AudioAsk aloud, hear a reply, and follow highlighted words.
VisualConnect the word with an illustration and image context.
InteractiveLet the child’s curiosity guide the next turn.

03 / Where we invested our time

Performance and interaction
need equal attention

01 / BACKEND ENGINEERING

Fast enough.
Good enough to teach.

Benchmark models and runtime designs. Compare quality, latency, memory, and device compatibility.

The result: evidence for which configuration to use.

02 / PRODUCT DESIGN

A conversation
that feels natural.

Prototype how children listen, speak, read, and interrupt. Make useful output arrive earlier.

The result: less perceived waiting and clearer control.

The product experience depends on both the model’s performance and the way we deliver its response.

04 / Measurement

Benchmarks that inform
product decisions

01

Model throughput

Fixed input and output lengths make runtime comparisons repeatable.

Initialization, first token, prefill, and decode. Warm-ups stay out of summaries.

02

Real interactions

Streaming prompts expose the wait a user actually experiences.

Time to first visible text, engine reuse, and the complete response.

03

Visual quality

A fixed 30-word image suite helps compare illustrations and generation time.

Save images, quality ratings, failures, and run history for review.

Every result needs contextModel hash, backend, device, workload, runtime, and thermal state.

Synthetic throughput does not measure teaching quality. Small run counts are exploratory, and failed or skipped samples are reported separately.

05 / The runtime

LiteRT gives us a path
to hardware acceleration

GPU and Tensor TPU support make faster local inference possible when the model, artifact, and device are compatible.

CPU

A working baseline for compatibility, output quality, and memory.

All four active image pipelines completed CPU smoke runs on the tested Tensor G5 phone.

GPU

A candidate for reducing inference time with compatible graphs.

Current compact SD-Turbo / SDXL-Turbo exports fail GPU compilation on the tested phone.

TPU

A device-specific path through matching Tensor artifacts and runtime support.

Gemma E2B integration exists. Image TPU execution still needs a validated compiled bundle.

Acceleration is an opportunity to measure. A successful conversion or capability check alone does not establish a speedup.

06 / Making models usable

The litert-cli skill helps us
adapt unsupported models

We use the skill in our conversion workflow and LiteRT CLI for quantization.

  1. Find a compatible artifact, or export the model’s components.
  2. Quantize and package the graphs for the phone.
  3. Check outputs, memory, and runtime behavior on the device.

SD-Turbo download size

Previous FP32 bundle5.03 GB
Compact INT8 / FP16 bundle1.32 GB

74%smaller download, approximately

SDXL-Turbo also fell from 13.75 GB to 3.53 GB.

Source: project quantization audit, 24 October 2026. Decimal GB for runtime files. Download size does not equal peak memory or prove accelerator compatibility.

08 / Perceived speed

Useful output can arrive
before the model finishes

Wait for the complete replyDelivery at the end
The child waits for the full answer.
Speak sentence by sentenceEarlier useful output
The first sentence can begin sooner.
Illustrative sequence, not a latency benchmark

Stream complete sentences
Queue speech while the rest of the reply is still generating.

Reuse the engine
Avoid paying initialization costs on every turn.

Keep context work in the background
Cache image descriptions and prioritize the child’s next question.

The animation illustrates delivery order only. It does not measure speech latency or a proven improvement in engagement.

09 / Intentional product design

A child should understand
what happens next

Clear turns

The assistant speaks, then listens. Visible states explain when it is listening, thinking, or talking.

Immediate control

Talk, Done, Cancel, and Stop speaking match the current stage of the conversation.

Speech with readable text

Short answers and word highlighting connect what a child hears with what they see.

A focused experience

Keep the screen awake during an active turn. Stop audio and inference when the child leaves.

These behaviors exist in the prototype. Fluency, voice detection, and learning value need evaluation with children on real devices.

10 / Decisions from the work

Benchmarks and prototypes
help us choose the combination

Evidence or constraintChoice it supportsWhat we defer
Recurring cloud cost limits accessLocal Gemma and local speech after provisioningA required cloud call for every learning turn
Image generation takes timePrepared illustrations and cached visual contextGenerating a new image during every reply
Compatibility varies by artifactExplicit backend checks and device measurementsAssuming every converted graph runs on GPU or TPU
A complete answer can arrive lateShort replies and sentence-level speech streamingHolding all output until generation ends

The first row follows our cost assumption. The remaining choices reflect prototype behavior and observed runtime constraints.

The ambition

A learning companion

On-device Gemma brings the intelligence closer.

The next proof

and evaluate learning experiences with children.
